subject: RE: Acme competitive evaluation + incident response / SLA comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: competitive eval + incident response follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery / competitive-eval conversation and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Primary evaluation goals (from Acme): performance at 1–2k TPS for embeddings and batch text generation; predictable 99th percentile latency for single-request inference; reproducible error handling and RCA timelines for incidents.

2) Competitive notes you flagged during the call: 
  - Acme is running tests against hyperscaler managed endpoints (Vertex/Sagemaker) and a few inference API vendors. Your main concerns were: outage windows, speed of escalation, and whether vendors provide meaningful RCAs with reproducible traces/logs.

3) Redwood differentiators we discussed: 
  - Dedicated routing and escape hatch to smaller-quantized model variants to maintain availability during high load.
  - Per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdowns in Console to speed RCA and quantify impact.
  - Clear escalation path with 24/7 SLA support tiers for Dedicated customers and an incident playbook we can share.

4) Proposed immediate next steps: 
  - Connor will share a short load-test plan (attachment) we suggest running in parallel against Redwood and your current endpoints (Vertex/SageMaker). That plan includes the exact payloads, sequence lengths, and traffic patterns we want to replicate.
  - Acme to share a sanitized sample of logs and typical payload distribution (if possible) so we can pre-configure batching/quantization suggestions.
  - We’ll provide our incident playbook and a mapping of SLAs/expected RCA timelines vs what you’ve seen from hyperscalers.
  - Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk through the test results and proposed mitigations.

Attachments: acme-load-test-plan.pdf (Connor) — please confirm you received.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate dates once I have availability from your side.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0119

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: competitive eval + incident response follow-up

Nicely written recap — adding a couple items from my side: 

- Pricing/commit considerations: if Acme wants Dedicated reserved capacity for the production path, we can map expected unit economics after the load run. That helps compare to hyperscaler egress + instance costs.
- Escalation SLA detail: for Dedicated we offer a priority response window (15 mins ack, 2-hour mitigation target) for P0s as an add-on. For hosted API tier, standard support is 4-hour business-day response. We should be explicit which mode Acme is planning to test.

Proposed quick agenda for the technical deep-dive: 
  1) Review load test methodology + run plan (Connor)
  2) Live comparison of 99p latency and cold-start behavior (Connor + Marissa)
  3) Incident simulation: how each provider surfaces traces, and expected RCA artifacts and timelines (Aditya)

Alice — are you leaning toward testing on hosted API first or going straight to Dedicated? Knowing that will determine escalation SLAs we show.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal AE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: competitive eval + incident response follow-up

Hi all — attaching the load test plan (acme-load-test-plan.pdf). Summary of the plan below and a short checklist so we can run both Redwood and Vertex/SageMaker tests in parity: 

Summary: 20 minute ramp to target, 30 minute steady-state at target TPS, two traffic patterns (single-request low-latency and batched throughput). Payloads reflect your average 512-token requests for generation + 1024-dim embeddings.

Checklist for parity: 
  - Provide sanitized sample payloads and header patterns.
  - Confirm target instance types/endpoint configs for hyperscalers (we’ll provide recommended Redwood config).
  - Agree on metric collection: 50/90/95/99p latencies, error-rate by code, request traces for 5 sampled failures.

Incident simulation notes: we’ll include a short P0 scenario where we saturate KV cache to reproduce a token-drop or memory-pressure event; the goal is to compare visibility into traces, ability to replay requests and time-to-RCA.

Attachment: acme-load-test-plan.pdf (1 page)

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: competitive eval + incident response follow-up

Marissa / team — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick notes from Acme: 

- We’ll start with hosted API parity tests against Vertex and Redwood (do not need Dedicated reserved capacity for the first evaluation).
- Security will provide sanitized payloads by EOD Tuesday.
- On SLAs: security is particularly interested in the actual RCA artifacts we can expect. With our current hyperscaler provider, RCAs are often high-level and take 7–10 business days for a detailed timeline. We need to understand whether Redwood provides reproducible traces and a clear timeline sooner.

Next steps: please run the parity tests and provide an incident comparison doc that lists: typical response windows, expected RCA contents (timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, reproducible traces/log samples), and any escalation contacts. Also please include the Redwood incident-playbook.pdf if you can.

—Alice
Alice Johnson
Engineering Manager, Data Platform — Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acme.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: competitive eval + incident response follow-up

Thanks — looped in. A few internal notes for the playbook and what we’ll share with Acme: 

- Playbook: include our standard timeline for Hosted vs Dedicated (Hosted: 4-hour business-day ack, 3–5 business day RCA; Dedicated: 15-min ack, 2 business day full RCA with reproducible traces where possible).
- Artifacts: include sample trace export, token-level latency breakdown, and the exact set of logs we can provide to customers (redacted).
- Escalation contacts: list a primary on-call, a secondary engineering lead, and a sales escalation owner (Aditya).

Marissa — please send the incident-playbook.pdf (redwood-incident-playbook.pdf) and I’ll approve a short customer-facing incident-comparison doc that directly contrasts Redwood vs typical hyperscaler practices for the security team.

Ben Carter
Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
